en: Chan Master Jishi was at Nanshan. I once met him;
his countenance was full and dignified, and his speech was piercing and sharp. As a fellow native of my own region, I loved him;
as a man of great reputation, I revered him. He has long been in stillness. His attendant is Chen Huijing.
Chè then requested that I provide a commentary on this record. I said: "The phrase 'having a phrase and lacking a phrase is like a vine leaning against a tree';

explaining it horizontally or vertically is like the moon reflected in rippling water. Since you, Master, have already provided such a thorough account and revealed yourself in such a manner, how can I possibly offer any further clarification?
Nevertheless, you once studied under Zhejiang Weng seven times, and in the end, it was due to the public case of Huanglong’s Three Barriers."

Thus he managed to have his nostrils knocked off by a single punch from Master Zhe-weng. There was something so magnificent about this, and such a sense of decisive resolution that it remains inexhaustible for him to draw upon throughout his life.
Yet, wishing to entrust it to future generations, in the end, to whom does it truly belong? Is it Jishi? Is it Master Zhe-weng? Or is it Huanglong? As the ancients said:
"If a single character is transcribed three times, how could it not turn 'ya' into 'ma'? How much more so when...
There are those with inscriptions on stone monuments above, and there are those with explanatory notes below;
do not mistake black beans for your own eyes, for then the wooden horse will neigh in the wind and the clay ox will enter the sea.
Written on the fifteenth day of the intercalary first month of the Wuchen year of the Xianchun era by Lin Xi-yi, known as Zhuxi and Yanzhai.

A Brief Record of the Ritual for Praising the Buddha and Patriarchs by Master Jishi,
upon his Initial Residence at Luohan Chan Temple on Mount Yan in Wenzhou.
Compiled by the student Zhengxian.
On the third day of the second month in the second year of the Shaoding era, the Master entered the monastery. Pointing to the triple gate, he said: "No solitary peril is established;
there is nothing hidden or concealed. With arms swinging, he walks on; pushing open the door, he enters the mortar."

The Buddha Hall. The Buddha-body is unconditioned; it does not fall within the realm of numerical categories. A clod of earth, a lump of mud, a lantern, and a pillar—incense is offered and it is said:
"The phoenix does not perch upon the wutong tree."
Seated upon the square measure of the abbot’s quarters, a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jun load will not trigger its mechanism for a mere field mouse.
To be pushed toward a precipice ten thousand *ren* high, one must first cast off one's body and surrender one's life. [The Master] pats the meditation seat and says: "Save your eyebrows!"
[The Master] pointed to the Dharma seat. "Those who ascend higher with every step do not lift their feet; those who do not lift their feet ascend higher with every step.
[He asked: "And what about the Korean Arhat? [Jizhou] said, "One, two, three, four, five," and then ascended the seat. Holding up the incense, he said:
"This one offering of incense is respectfully offered to extend [the Emperor's] longevity..."
May the present Emperor’s sacred person enjoy ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years!

May Your Majesty, the Emperor, reverently be granted the longevity of a dynasty and its generations, further anticipating the long duration of the Zhou calendar; may you have many years of life and many sons, so that we may offer the blessings of Hua, Feng, and Zhong.
Next, holding up the incense, he says: "From Zhongfu and Taibai to Lingxiao; from the youth Xue to the elder Dao at Dongshan on two occasions.
The Buddha’s hand is a favorable affinity, while the donkey’s feet are a painful blow—a single fist that reveals the beggar’s state of utter poverty.
I burn this in the incense burner to honor the late Abbot of Jingshan Xingxing Wanshou Chan Monastery, the State-Specially-Appointed Chan Master Foxin, the Great Zeweng."
The Master, wishing to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk, took his seat and said: "In the Great Peace there are no signs; in the Way of Kings there is no partiality.
With the halting of arms and weapons, it is precisely the time for us to meet. A monk asked, "At the bottom of the deep Dragon Abyss, the horns and head protrude with imposing majesty;
atop the peaks of Mount Yandang, the *dharma-flower* manifests as a portent. What is the phrase that benefits others? The Master said, "A numinous tortoise suddenly emerges."
"Supreme Peak. The student said, "In that case, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace are both repaid at once. The Master said, "I thank you, Kalyāṇamitra, for your testimony.
The student said, "Sansheng said, 'Whenever I meet a person, I come forth; yet when I come forth, it is not for the sake of others. What does this mean?
The Master said, "Seeking a pearl by draining the ocean. The student said, "Xinghua said, 'Whenever I meet a person, I do not come forth; yet when I come forth...'"

[The monk] said, "Then he becomes a person. The Master said, "Climbing the mountain to hold up the moon. [The monk] stepped forward and asked, "When these two great elders speak in such a manner, how far apart are they?
The Master said, "In the same spring breeze, there are flowers of a hundred varieties. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further above this?
The Master said, "Among them all, this scene is difficult to capture in a painting. The monk rubbed his forehead and said, "Today I have personally seen Nāgārjuna."
The Venerable Luo asked, "Master, [the Buddha] is still separated by the sea. The Master said, "He is still separated by the sea.

The monk pressed further, "What can be done? The Buddha’s hand is difficult to shield. The Master said, "Prostrate yourself. The monk prostrated. The Master then said, "The entrustment at Vulture Peak."
Yellow leaves to stop a child’s crying; the mind at rest at Shaoshi. Shouldering snow to fill a well—one error leads to a hundred errors. This error persists to this very day.
Upādyāya Peng, in your ordinary life by the waterside and beneath the forest trees, you sought nothing from the sages and harbored no longing for your own spiritual brilliance.
Who cared for heaven? Who cared for earth? Without cause, you lost your footing and fell into this crowd. You can do no more than take what is wrong and make it right.
"Wrong! You have gone off into the thicket of brambles, leaping here and there at will, to commit this sinful karma. [The Master] strikes the meditation seat and says:
"A single moon rises over the sea; how many families ascend the tower? [The Master] cites an ancient worthy who asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Xuefeng.
The ancient worthy said, "When I arrived there back then, everything was insufficient. Now it is sufficient."

"Not yet," the monk said. "Enough," the ancient worthy replied. "Porridge is enough; rice is enough. The monk remained silent. The Master said, "Only when one does not covet the fragrant bait is one a true scaled dragon;
only when one does not fall into the net is one a true auspicious beast. This monk did not know how to hide his body and brought trouble upon the ancient worthy, who once again laid down a trap.
Do you wish to know? When there is no concern, one naturally follows the current; when there is sound, it mostly leads to..."
An informal discourse on the arrival of the Uneven.
To raise one thing, one must not raise two; let this one point pass. Holding up his staff, he said:
"The Venerable Nāgārjuna has arrived! From the crest of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, he unleashes a torrent—like thunder, like a crash of lightning, like an electric flash, like mist."
Like a jewel, like sleet, like a rainbow, like rain—hundreds of thousands of millions of transformations, without end.
All the people in the world stare with wide-open eyes at this point; yet even if one were to penetrate through the precipice and cut off the source, one would still not have met the Venerable One.
How much more so for us monks—there is still a distance of thousands and tens of thousands of miles. (He plants his staff.)
Zhaozhou said: "The clouds move and the rain falls; there are the three types of grass and two kinds of trees.

Yangshan once suddenly saw a strange monk arrive through the air and stand before him. Yangshan asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "This morning I left the Western Heaven."

Yangshan said, "Why were you born so late? The monk said, "I have been traveling through the mountains and enjoying the waters. Yangshan said, "Your spiritual powers and wondrous functions are indeed not lacking, O Kalyāṇamitra;

however, as for the Buddha-dharma, it must be returned to this old monk. The monk said, "I came specifically to this Eastern Land to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet I have instead encountered a 'lesser Śākyamuni.
He then produced a *bēṭa* leaf from Western India, prostrated before Yangshan, and departed through the air. The Master said:
Jin said that this monk comes from empty space and goes into empty space; he did not cut off his heels to make him return home and sit securely, but was instead met with two ladles of foul water.
Little did he know that, having been squeezed by Yangshan twice, the monk simply ran east and west, calling a bell a jar.
Had Jin carried out his instructions, there would have been no one capable of taking them up.

As the two classes of monks take their places on the platform, before the sound of the voice and after the phrase, there is total release and total gathering; as the constellations shift and the stars change, it is half-lit and half-dark.
Yet, while we strive to enjoy this era of peace and prosperity, none can deceive the assembly. Why? Because one must adapt to local customs when entering a village.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In Uttarakuru to the north and Aparagoyānī to the west, whether there is profit or loss, one never leaves the marketplace.
Holding up his staff, he said: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take away your staff.
Leaning on the staff, he said: "The Boatman went down to Yangzhou; gold and silver were like dross. He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: One lamp branches into lamps, yet the lamps are inexhaustible; one place is bright, and everywhere it penetrates simultaneously.
Amidst the bustling clamor, not a single dharma is abandoned; in the profound stillness, not a single speck of dust is admitted. This is the "leakage" of the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
Ascending the hall on the fifteenth day of the second month: the affairs of spring are in full bloom. Even the Yellow-Faced Old Man has not yet severed his life-root.
At this very moment, life and death rest in the hands of everyone present. Those who have no sinews in their eyes and no blood beneath their skin—listen to another decree!
(He raises the whisk and says: "Today there is; tomorrow there is not."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "For thirty years, Lingyun spoke only of 'no doubt,' yet he had never truly recognized the face of the peach blossoms.

Xuan Sha said, 'How profoundly true, how most true! yet I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the end; you are still like one supporting himself while crossing a bridge in a drunken stupor."
It is just like when Fenyang heard this and could not help but laugh heartily. What does this mean? "The road enters the Peach Blossom Spring;
it grows deeper and deeper. [He] ascended the hall and said:
"In essence, we belong to one family, yet there are ten thousand divergences and a thousand differences. Yunmen’s 'millet cake,' Zhaozhou’s 'tea. [He] threw down [his staff]."
[The Master] held up his staff and said, "How does it compare to the turtle-nosed snake of the Southern Mountain?
He ascended the hall and raised the following case: When Zhenjing was ascending the hall, he said, "The Head-dhuta Rock is enveloped in moss; Peak Pen-thrown is entangled by *pǐlì* vines.
At Luohan Temple, three novices are ordained every year. At Guizong, after the formal session has ended, they drink tea. The Master [then spoke].
He said: "I shall not ask about the Zen of the Tathāgata or the Zen of the Patriarchs. But tell me, why does ginger never lose its pungency?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Known before it is raised; understood before it is spoken. Zhaozhou has no gate; Xuansha has a ridge.
He struck his staff down and said: "Ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences are settled by a single seal."
The Buddha’s Birthday. The Master ascends the hall and cites the story of Śākyamuni pointing to heaven and pointing to earth, saying, "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
Yunmen said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog, just to ensure peace throughout the world.
The Master says, "Śākyamuni, at the very end, acted as an unsurpassed and fearless great lion."
The Lion’s Roar! Clearly, this is a scene of war upon level ground. Although Yunmen exhausted his loyal heart and courageous spirit in surrendering to righteousness, he sought only to secure peace;
yet in doing so, he further stirred up chaos within the universe. Had the Arhat seen this at that time, he would have immediately said: "Lower your voice! Lower your voice!"
Furthermore, tell me: what principle does this rely upon? Even the sovereigns Yao and Shun still had their transformations to bring about.
Entering the hall [for the sermon]: On the fifth day of the fifth month, the Festival of Midsummer. A patch-robed monk’s shout is like a thunderbolt; his staff falls like raindrops.
Atop a solitary peak, he scolds and reviles as he pleases. What do you call "red-mouthed and white-tongued"? When encountering a Buddha, he kills the Buddha; when encountering...
The Patriarch kills the Patriarch; meeting an Arhat, he kills the Arhat. What do you call this "evil vapor" or "demonic sprite"?
He brandishes his staff and says: "This one divine talisman is not obtained from others. At such a time as this, bring me back my lion cub!"
Master Fahong ascended the hall. A gale-force wind and torrential rain raged uncontrollably; rocks split and cliffs collapsed, leaving no time for escape.
Only when everyone’s worldly life has been utterly swept away will one truly see that the times are clear and the Way is prosperous. Holding up his staff, he said: "Merit is never bestowed in vain."
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: The autumn rain falls desolately; the autumn clouds are dark and gloomy. Raising his staff, he said: "Do you see it?
Eighty-four thousand chisels have been forged; it is not like the ordinary three or five full moons."
On the fifteenth day of the ninth month, he ascended the hall. At noon, it was the hour of midnight; a thousand gates and ten thousand doors were all wide open.
One sound, two sounds of the mortar and pestle: the drifting sands stretch across vast waves, the Onion Range offers no path. Since when did Bodhidharma ever return?
The first day of the eleventh month. Ascending the hall: The great earth is all frozen and locked; the entire world is as hot as fire.
The seasons do not let one pass by, yet many patch-robed monks miss the mark. Not missing it—there is one person amidst the deep snow who lets out a shout. (He lets out a shout.)
Master Xie received the supervision and ascended the hall. A sharp-witted monk acts without calculation;

mixing water with mud at the edge of the fields and by the side of the earth, he constructs it perfectly, yet he only obtains half. Since he has constructed it perfectly, why does he only obtain half?
A deep pit is difficult to fill.

On the arrival of the festival, he ascended the hall. His staff was coiled and bent; it turned the celestial pivot and shifted the terrestrial axis. The multitude of yin energies were being stripped away moment by moment;
the single yang energy returned day after day. Why is it that even Arhats find the Cold Gate within the mountains difficult to approach?
It is not that those who have not undergone bitter toil do not know.

Ascending the hall for the Imperial Birthday: Now, one who preaches the Dharma should preach in accordance with the Dharma. This morning, we inaugurate the ceremony for the Imperial Birthday of the Heavenly Foundation.

With a humble heart beneath this forest, I shall serve with total loyalty and integrity, preaching in accordance with the Dharma. All you members of the assembly before me, share in this same humble heart;
listen attentively, listen attentively! (Rising from his seat:)
May the Holy Personage live for ten thousand years!
On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascends the hall: his entire being sits within Mount Perfect Enlightenment. When he wishes to walk, he walks; when he wishes to act, he acts.
Where the morning star appears, the path is clear; with tenfold compassion, he accomplishes liberation from delusion.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year: Last night, the old year departed; today, the new year arrives.
The lanterns and the pillar do not fail to break into hearty laughter. But tell me, what are they laughing at? Bodhidharma sat facing the wall; Yunmen recited "seven."
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Furi Jinghui of Leping Mountain, Lin’an Prefecture;
Compiled by the Students. Pointing to the Three Gates, he said:
"This gate of ours has no path of approval at all. The threefold jeweled stairway is merely a concession made for the sake of this present age."
He gave a shout and said, "Step back! Step back!
The life of the Yellow-Faced Old Man in the Buddha Hall has today fallen into the hands of Venerable Peng.
To lift him up or cast him down is no mere matter."

Seated upon the square measure of the abbot’s quarters at the head of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, amidst the flash of lightning, he causes them to die and live together, before meeting again on another peak.

Having ascended the seat and finished the prayers for the Emperor (the question-and-answer session is not recorded), he said: "Great capacity and great function—whether fully raised or partially raised—he holds it fast."
Let it pass. There is guest and there is host; all is but the spreading of mats and the opening of the hall. From afar they hasten to catch the wind, first offering up their "dead" confessions.
Their shadows sink into cold water; they borrow the ground for a living burial. Within the context of the fundamental inquiry, there is as yet no room for buying or selling.
Merely to accord with the times, I shall state it clearly: On the road beneath Mount Linping in the fifth month, the lotus flowers have not yet bloomed.
The number [of years] was fulfilled at Dingzhou. When the Mountain was opened, Master Furi was at Jia Shan.
One day, during a communal work session (*pǔqǐng*), the Rector (*weina*) ordered Furi to deliver tea. Furi said, "I have come solely for the sake of the Buddha-Dharma; I have not come to deliver tea.
The Rector said, "The Abbot has commanded me to invite you, Senior Monk (*shàngzuò*). Furi said, "The Abbot may do as he pleases," and then he took the tea.

He went to the place where the work was being done and rattled his tea bowl to make a sound. Yunmen did not look back. Jiaofan said, "Three or five bowls of strong tea; the meaning lies at the edge of the mattock.

Yunmen said, "The pitcher has the momentum to pour the tea; how many bowls are in the basket? Jiaofan said, "The pitcher has the momentum to pour the tea; there is not a single bowl in the basket," and then he poured the tea and moved on.

At that time, the assembly looked up at him, and Jiaofan— *Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "Jiaofan" (日), which refers to Jiaofan Huiqin (夾山會稹), the master who engaged in this dialogue with Yunmen Wenyan (雲門文偃).*
The assembly looked up expectantly and requested a word from the Master. Xishan said, "If you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it;
carry it home in a bottomless basket. Dayu said, "Holding a night-bright talisman in one's hand, how many know the dawn?
Xishan called to the assembly, saying, "There is someone! Go back! Go back! The Master [Yunmen] said, "The Master may indeed attain it, but as for the side of the mattock..."
The matter has already been entrusted to Furi. Although there were people invited to pick tea, it turned out unfinished.
Nevertheless, although Jia Shan’s eyesight was sharp and clear, he knew that Furi had come from Yunju and did not treat him as a mere "little Wang Bao" making straw sandals. He looked after him.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas appearing in the world borrow water to offer flowers; the Patriarchs coming from the West cast their molds to produce bricks.
The entire Great Canon of Teachings is merely an examination essay; even clear-eyed monks end up leaning on fences and feeling along walls. But when it comes to this point, what is to be done?
I only wish that the silkworms and wheat may ripen this year, so that Rāhula’s son might be given a single coin."

Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year: Bodhidharma came from the West, yet he did not recognize the lines of the divination chart; his random and confused divinations have been passed down to this day.
Buddhadina and I are here opening a shop; dare we, before the signs have even begun to manifest, plant our staff? (He plants the staff.)
The first day of the first month in the first year of the Duanping era.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A thousand-fathom fishing line hangs straight down; when a single wave stirs, ten thousand waves follow. He took up his staff and said:
"You people here—how will you swallow this? Leaning on his staff, he said: 'Eating porridge and eating rice—what difficulty is there in that?
He gave a shout."
Ascending the hall: The peach blossoms are in full, riotous bloom; they are the blood in Lingyun’s eyes. Were it not for one whose heart is broken, to whom could this resentment be told?
Ascending the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday: As soon as he emerged from the womb, he scattered calamity upon the dust; even until now, he continues to harm people. One—
The ladle and scented bath harbor boundless regret; how could the weight on one’s wrists be less than a thousand pounds?
Entering the hall: During the summer retreat, when the feet are constrained, a single phrase is directly raised—pervading the earth and filling the heavens—on the fifteenth day of the fourth month.
Ascending the hall: "A single leaf falls, and autumn comes to all under heaven. For those who cannot avoid it, their eyes bulge out;
for those who have no way to peer into it, whether in the southern regions or the northern lands, there is a reason for its coming, yet there is no reason for its departure.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the tenth month: When the season arrives, its underlying principle naturally manifests.

Thus, when winter comes, water begins to freeze; when winter comes, the earth begins to harden; and when winter comes, the myriad things reach fruition. But as for the patch-robed monk when winter arrives—how is it then?
He is scorched first by the fire.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Winter is not yet cold; wait until after the year-end festival. A biting wind sweeps the earth, freezing the mud-clods to pieces.
Before the pavilions of Vairocana, amidst the deep snows of Shaolin—who would have known that we are still separated by ten thousand layers of gates? He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Stale goods have no price; rotten coins have no string. Clenching the teeth with determination, take what is wrong and make it right.
Heaven shall appoint you, Master, as the wooden clapper. He gave a shout.
Xie Liangban ascends the hall. Holding up a broken-legged cauldron, each extends a hand. Śākyamuni does not precede; Maitreya does not follow.
Wondrous function meets the occasion like a pearl rolling on a platter. Drumming his belly, he laughs and sings again: facing south, he gazes at the Big Dipper.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old precedent, saying: "An ancient master said, 'The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years to seek one who understands.
If you understand it in this way, there will come a day when you shall eat iron rods. Another old master said, "'The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years—how could he not feel ashamed?
If you understand it in this way, you must set aside money for straw sandals; you have been traveling on pilgrimage for thirty years. The Master said, "These two elders..."
Xiu: To speak in such a manner is very much like opening the gate of the Patriarchs and cutting off the path for those who come.
Since it is not thus, how is it ultimately? Bodhidharma faced the wall.
The Buddha ascends the hall after attaining enlightenment: For six years he buried his body in the grass; at that time, though he had eyes, they never once opened.
Truly, when he beheld the appearance of the morning star, He had not yet reached the gate where the courtyard is cold as ashes.
Record of the Sayings of Baofu Chan Temple on Mount Daimei in Qingyuan Prefecture.
Compiled by a Disciple. Buddha Hall:
Those who sit are killed by sitting; those who stand are killed by standing. Who knows which is the red-bearded barbarian? A phrase for turning back.
The fish is lively and darting.
[He] picks up the notice and says: "Within the treasury of our King, there is no such blade. He raises it and says: "A swift opportunity is hard to encounter; total killing, total life.
The Rector simply presents it in this manner.

He ascended the seat. After the prayer for the Emperor was concluded (the question-and-answer session is not recorded), he said: "From the time of the ancient ancestors, the unsurpassed, wondrous flavor has been treasured by the world.
Yet, before the flower-scented breeze had arrived, why did all the people of the great earth look toward plum trees to quench their thirst?
Therefore, at Huangmei, seven hundred [monks] plucked leaves and sought branches; at the three watches beneath the mortar, they shifted their nests and struck down their targets."
Reaching as far as the summit of Mount Dayu, where upon the branches and vines new branches and vines grow again: you say "neither mind nor Buddha," while I say "this very mind is Buddha.
This is no different from half-heartedly playing with colors like green and yellow. Master Mazu said, "The plum has ripened," yet it was all in vain to ferment such thoughts.
Layman Pang personally tested this himself; it is much like glue forming in one's mouth. Give me back the pit!
"Come! I shall ensure you cannot spit it out. [The Master] strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and says: "Today, everything has been smashed to pieces at once.
There is nothing that does not receive the power of the spring, and nothing that does not require cultivation; all are torn asunder. In the end, they will never be fragrant.
But how can one attain harmony between person and environment? After a long silence, he says: "The name comes from the precious cauldron’s tuning."
The soup is ready. Bending his way in, he plays the *huqiu* flute under the moon.

When Jue was inaugurating this mountain, Mazu sent a monk to inquire of him, saying, "How long have you been living on this mountain? Jue said, "I have only seen the four mountains turn green and then yellow.
The monk asked, "What principle did you realize that led you to live on this mountain? Jue said, "I was in Jiangxi."

Having received the essential teaching of "this very mind is Buddha" from Master Ma, he resided on this mountain. A monk said, "Lately, Master Ma’s understanding of the Buddha-dharma has changed. The founder asked, "How has it changed? The monk said, "It is 'neither mind nor Buddha'. The founder said, "Let him have 'neither mind nor Buddha'; as for me, I maintain 'this very mind is Buddha'. The monk returned to Jiangxi and informed Master Ma. Master Ma said, "This fellow has been living on that mountain for a long time; he will surely not change his ways. The monk went back to the mountain and reported what Master Ma had said. The founder laughed and said, "I knew he would not change. He then composed a verse: "The Great Way is originally not difficult; Just avoid picking and choosing. Neither mind nor Buddha, Nor even no-mind— The more you try to grasp it, The further away it goes. Later, when Master Ma heard of this, he sighed and said, "That fellow has indeed attained my marrow. The monk returned to Jiangxi and told Master Ma about the verse. Master Ma said, "This fellow has truly attained my marrow. He then composed a verse: "The Great Way is originally not difficult; Just avoid picking and choosing. Neither mind nor Buddha, Nor even no-mind— If you can understand this, Then you will see the Buddhas of the three times. Master Ma then sent a letter to the founder, saying: "My old man, you have attained my marrow. The founder replied: "I have attained your skin and flesh, but I have not yet attained your marrow. Master Ma said, "You have attained my marrow. The monk returned to the mountain and reported this. The founder said, "I knew he would not change.
