Like a golden-winged bird cleaving the sea, or a raging thunderclap shattering a mountain. Holding up his staff, he said: "I and you were born of the same root."
I will not die with you on the same path. Climbing a mountain, one must reach its peak; entering the sea, one must reach its bottom. The *mingpeng* bird spans ninety thousand *li*;
the *liaohè* crane has three thousand years. One must know that the seas and mountains return to the enlightened lord; it is not necessarily that heaven and earth fall upon the auspicious person.
Again, Huangshan went to Jia Shan. Jia Shan asked, "Where are you from? Huangshan said, "From Min. Jia Shan said, "Have you..."
“Do you recognize this old monk? Huang said, “Do you recognize this student? Jiashan said, “Let us set this matter aside for now;
give me back the price of my straw sandals, and I shall give you back the price of rice in Jiangling. Huangshan said, “What is the price of rice in Jiangling?
Jiashan said, “A true lion cub; he knows how to roar the lion’s roar. The Master said, “Huangshan took advantage of the opportunity to open the door.”

With no way to turn back, Jia Shan’s questioning was thorough and discerning, while Daoli’s responses were merely evasive. At that time, had he waited for the question, "What is the price of rice in Jiangling?
he would have taken up his staff and struck him immediately.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Those who sit in a deep well do not know the vastness of the great void; only those who have cast away biased views can understand the perfect integration of the ultimate principle.
Deshan arrived from the south carrying his commentaries and sub-commentaries, his bearing like that of a king.
I do not ask why he burned [the texts] in Longtan’s mountain retreat, but why, upon seeing a monk enter the gate, did he immediately strike him? When one is poor, one's wisdom is short."

Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Dongshan asked Qinglin, "Where have you recently come from? Qinglin said, "Wulin. Dongshan said, "How does the Dharma-way of Wulin compare to this place? Qinglin said, "Sprouts growing in winter on foreign soil.

Dongshan said, "I shall cook fragrant rice in a separate steamer as an offering. Qinglin then went out. Dongshan remarked, "This fellow will run the people of the world to death in the future. The Master said: The Master said: "If one has not yet attained the Way, one must first seek it; once the Way is attained, one must not dwell upon it.

To dwell upon it is to fall into the pit of views; to seek it is to fall into the pit of seeking. To avoid these two pitfalls, one must transcend both attainment and non-attainment. Only then can one be called a true person of the Way. But tell me, where does one find such a person? Look! He is right here, right now, in the midst of the assembly. He struck the meditation seat once and descended.

Discerning gold from jade, he restores to others the clarity and precision of their own eyes. Even if one stands directly amidst the green forest and refuses offerings of fragrant incense from another steamer, one still encounters two ladles of foul water from him.
On the Double Ninth, the Master ascended the hall: "Before my old monk’s porch, yellow chrysanthemums are beyond counting, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Who is at the painted pavilion where wine is bought? Come, they invite you to drink Zhaozhou’s tea."

Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth month: Six years in the Snowy Mountains, he deceived himself; yet there, amidst the bright stars in the azure heavens, with eyes wide open, there was no place for evasion.
Throughout the heavens and across the earth, all was dark and vast. The sun and moon of antiquity and today; the stars and constellations of antiquity and today.
[The Master] held up his whisk and said, "Do you see? After a long silence, he said, "If one were to shed tears frequently, even the vast ocean would surely dry up.
He ascended the hall and, citing the public instruction of Jiufeng, said: "The eternally abiding Dharmakāya is neither born nor does it perish.
A monk then asked, "Since it is neither born nor does it perish, why do beings transmigrate through the six realms? Jiufeng replied, "It is because of the existence of the mind. The monk said:
"By what means shall one realize the Dharmakāya? Feng said, "By means of the mind of emptiness, one unites with the principle of emptiness.
The monk asked, "What is it like after realization? Feng said, "Let the three realms revolve as they will; let the four modes of birth rush about in vain. He added, "Do you understand?"
The monk said, "I do not understand. Feng said, "Pay your respects. The Master remarked, "Jiufeng was quite like one skilled in the Kaishu (regular) script;
every stroke and dot was distinct and clear. Yet, when this monk said 'I do not understand,' he produced a cursive (Caoshu) script instead.
Nevertheless, if there is no cursive script within one's breast, it is difficult to appreciate the calligraphic works of Wang Xizhi and Wang Xianzhi."
Record of the Sayings of Baolin Chan Temple on Mount Yunhuang in Wuzhou, compiled by Attendants Zongtan and Yanhui.
Pointing to the Main Gate, he said: "This great pavilion has neither abiding nor departing; this pavilion gate has neither opening nor closing."
The authors all return together; no effort is required for even a snap of the fingers.
In Maitreya’s Hall, they are led before the Seven Buddhas and followed behind Vimalakīrti. Knowing only how to follow the ranks and pursue the heterodox, when has their heel ever touched the ground?
Spreading out the sitting mat, he says: "Look, look! Covering the earth and covering the heavens, it is now being circulated!"
Holding up the notice: To see it upon first sight; once attained, it is attained forever. Held forth in the open light, it moves like thunder and blows like wind.
The Monastery Preface: Departing from the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations—listen to the primary truth.

Pointing to the Dharma-seat: when practice reaches it but teaching does not, there is leaking rain and leaking wind; when teaching reaches it but practice does not, one bumps into walls and crashes into barriers.
What is it like when both practice and teaching reach it? There is still something further above.

Ascending the seat, he offered prayers for the Emperor. (The question and answer are not recorded. He then said: "Striking the door-mallet and tapping the sounding-block, the clanging of blades resounds throughout the entire world."
Thorny brambles reaching the heavens. Such and such. In the place of the furnace and bellows, not such and such.
Even the Buddha’s hand cannot shield it. When none of these apply, what then? Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind upon this long ago; until this very day, he has not attained the wondrous.
Quoting Chan Master Xuedou Mingjue’s address to the assembly: "Mountains and rivers have no obstruction; light..."
"Clear through every place. Great Master Fu rides his donkey into your nostrils. Seeing that people are not alert, he returns to Shuanglin Temple.
He then descended from the seat. The Master said, "For Xuedou to speak in this way, it is easy to deceive people, but difficult to bury them.
Why? Because when you go out the door, you see mountains and rivers; when you enter the gate, you see..."

In the Buddha Hall, he ascended the seat and raised up the example of the Great Master Fu, who wore a Daoist crown, Confucian shoes, and a Buddhist *kāṣāya*. When he appeared before Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, the Emperor asked, "Are you a monk?
The Master pointed to his crown. The Emperor said, "Is it the Way? The Master pointed to his shoes. The Emperor said, "Are you a layperson? The Master pointed to his *kāṣāya*.

Fenyang said, "The Great Being is capable of much. Wuzu Jie said, "The bystander looks on with disapproval. The Master said, "Emperor Wu held up his sacred mirror high, wishing to see black and white clearly distinguished.
The Great Being met him face-to-face and responded directly; it was certainly not a matter of asking for salt or offering fodder for a horse.
When examined closely, he only knew how to sell the expensive, but did not know how to sell the cheap. What a pity! At that time, Emperor Wu let him go."
[The Master] said, "It has passed. He then gave him a sharp rebuke: "Neither monk, nor Way, nor layman—what else could it be?
He would certainly have left him with a parched mouth and a swollen tongue.
Ascending the hall, he said: "First, you must not point toward it; second, you must not seek it. Strolling idly in the corridor, sitting in meditation in the hall—look into your own eyes!"
[The Master] says, "In the ear! Guanyin Hudamo. He strikes the meditation seat and says, "Pass!

On the occasion of the opening of the summer retreat, he ascends the hall: "Grasping the bright pearl from the dragon's jaw, wielding the Vajra jewel-sword, day after day observing the foot-restraint of *an-gu* (the summer retreat)."
Each and every one has attained the "Pass" with an empty mind; yet this remains merely the ordinary conduct of a patch-robed monk.

Having only recently entered the monastery at Śāla Grove, I dare not go against worldly custom or violate the timing of the age. Therefore, as I descend from my seat, let us together with all people here perform a universal prostration.

On the birthday of the Great Being Shan-hui, he ascended the hall and said: "The ocean of compassionate vows and the ocean of the four modes of birth emerge and submerge, unfold and contract, with perfect interfusion and sovereign mastery.
Holding up his staff, he said: "The Great Being Shan-hui arrives! Even the flash of a spark or a streak of lightning must be set aside to one side."
Just as he was about to lift his eyes, [he spoke: "At the Dragon Flower Assembly, leaning on my staff, I descend from the seat. He ascends the hall.
"During the holy regulation of the summer retreat, this mountain monk has been abroad for over a month. Crossing ridges and following mountains, passing through fields and piercing through paths;
when a great road was reached, I entered deep villages again. Wishing to go to that other side, I cut across the stream without a second thought. Nevertheless—"
Not following the holy regulations, yet there is one who understands. Tell me, who is this one who understands? *Namo* Heart-King Bodhisattva.
(This was said while a thief had been caught in the hall. At the third watch of the night, when heaven is dark and earth is black, right beside this mass of red flesh, a thief has been caught.
It would be fitting to give him three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening; yet suddenly, he slips from the hands of the "white-handed" thief and divides the loot.

"How is it at such a time? "Thief! Thief! He ascended the hall and cited Master Fu Dashi, who said: "Night after night one embraces the Buddha in sleep; morning after morning one rises together with him.

Rising and sitting, we always follow one another; speaking and remaining silent, we dwell together. Not a single hair's breadth separates us; they are like a body and its shadow. If you wish to know the Buddha..."
"As for the place where he went, it was simply this sound of his voice. Xuansha said, "The Great Master Fu Da Shi recognized nothing more than that which is bright and alert.
Xuedou said, "Xuansha was merely striking the grass to startle the snake. The Master said, "The Great Master let go."
Thus, this [state] is riddled with holes from every side; it has been pierced by you. When the Great Being seizes hold of it, where else can one turn one's gaze?
After a long silence, he said: "Wait until the descent into birth."

Ascending the hall during Midsummer: Heaven attains the center as the stars and constellations are arrayed; Earth attains the center as yin and yang harmonize. When a patch-robed monk attains the center, he lays down his weapons.
Yet, following the cold and pursuing the heat, one merely stirs up a fuss for oneself. This summer consists of ninety days, and today is Midsummer.
Why is it that when you have not yet raised a question, you already offer a response? And why, when asked, "What is your mind?", do you again fail to answer?
[The Master] said, "Understood. He took up his staff and said, "When this staff reaches this point, it cannot be without fault.
Do you all know how to feel the pain and the itch? He gave a shout.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The sacred regulations for the summer retreat are a path different from that of ordinary people. Holding up his staff, he said: "The past cannot be apprehended;
the present cannot be apprehended; the future cannot be apprehended. To overturn the pavilions of Vairocana takes but a moment.
Above the heavens there is no Maitreya; beneath the earth there is no Maitreya."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Throughout the entire universe and the great earth, all the buddhas as numerous as motes of dust contend for the Buddha-dharma upon the tip of this staff, seeking victory and defeat.
National Teacher Yunmen, since opening up his own domain, has let this staff fight and strike with Maitreya and Śākyamuni.
Master Langya was much like one who failed to settle the host; picking up the staff, he said: 'This one...'"
"This is the staff. Which one among these is the myriad Buddhas, Maitreya, or Śākyamuni? He planted the staff in the ground and said, "Torn asunder!

On the first day of the eighth month, he ascended the hall, beckoned with his hand, and strode across transversely. "How could it be made into a dragon when held up? It blows forth right before one's eyes."
The cloth-hair arises; mistaking orange peel for fire. A gust of autumn wind arrives, and two or three leaves fall.
The money for gruel and the money for straw sandals—having no choice but to do so—I have now returned them to you all.
From Western India to Eastern China, the Chang’an Road grows beneath the feet of every person. *Hah!* (A shout).
Ascending the hall, he said: "To dwell in existence is to destroy existence; to dwell in emptiness is to destroy emptiness. Once both illusions are removed, the Middle Way cannot be established.
For you monks, put on your straw sandals tightly. When you suddenly turn around and breathe freely here, what then?
Reaching the river where the land of Wu ends, beyond the bank are many mountains of Yue."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "All obstacles are ultimate awakening. In the mountains, rivers, and the great earth; in the sun, moon, and stars;

in the myriad phenomena arrayed before us, and in light, darkness, form, and emptiness—where is there any obstacle? In walking, standing, sitting, and reclining; in blinking the eyes and raising the eyebrows;
in spreading out the bedding and unfolding the bowl; in moving about, turning, bowing, and looking up—where is there any obstacle? But ultimately, what is it that one awakens to?"
To awaken, and yet to ask what it is that one awakens to—this "all-knowledge wisdom" (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
Śākyamuni the Old Man deserves thirty blows of the staff for this!

Taking his place upon the high seat, he addressed the assembly: "The old trees have formed a lofty forest; in the autumn sky, the bright moon appears. Within a mustard seed, one enters right concentration;

from Mount Sumeru, one emerges from that concentration. The Buddhas of the past, the Buddhas of the present, and the Buddhas of the future—there is nothing that can be compared to them. How am I to explain this?"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Before the auspicious markings have appeared on the sacred tortoise, and before the black beans have sprouted—if you can utter a single phrase that covers the earth and encompasses the heavens, it still would not be the 'Teacherless Phrase' or the 'Natural Phrase.
The autumn wind is high; the autumn sky is vast. When did Xuefeng ever break through the bottom of his bucket?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "No Buddha, no sentient beings, no past, no present. He struck the left side of the meditation seat and said, "Pass over here!
"No cultivation, no realization, no conditioned action. He struck the right side of the meditation seat and said, "Pass over here! Then he held up his whisk and said:
"Do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "The whole lump cannot be split; I give you two coins.
When Fo Chengdao ascended the hall, he said: "The stars in heaven appear night after night; only when the eyes are opened wide does one finally see them.
The Yellow-Faced Gautama has had the arrow pulled from behind his head."
Ascending the hall, he said: "All Buddhas and sentient beings alike rely upon this power of grace.
As for us patch-robed monks, with a pint and three gills carried at the tip of our staffs, we walk when we wish to walk and sit when we wish to sit. Furthermore, what power of grace do we rely upon?
After a long silence, he said: "Eating porridge, eating rice."
Ascending the hall, he said: "In cold weather, they freeze to death; in hot weather, they scorch to death. Everywhere, people are universally engaged in the seasonal greetings of cold and heat.

At Shuanglin, in cold weather we scorch to death, and in hot weather we freeze to death. This is not at all a change of principle. Why? Because from the beginning, the Great Being has worn his crown upon his head."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The three realms offer no peace; they are like a burning house. The gate of a skilled physician is frequented by many sick people.
Great Master Fu lost his nostrils and eyes, and to this day they cannot be found.
Lord Hu, however, insisted on building a temple atop a high mountain peak, regardless of whether salt was expensive or rice was cheap. A gust of spring wind arrives, and three or five flowers bloom."
A fragment. The Great Master Bodhidharma could not gain entry through his greetings; suddenly, he took a single shoe and returned to the Western Heaven. (He lets out a shout. Entering the hall:
"The true essence of the teaching in this land is pure and still within hearing. Within the eyes and within the ears, there is absolutely no point of contact.
"Thirty blows of the staff from Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, banished beyond the Iron Ring Mountains—this is true diligence;
this is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata."

Ascending the hall: When one place is penetrated, a thousand places and ten thousand places are entirely free from entanglement. The green mountains are ever-present, yet true knowledge is difficult to encounter.
Before the time of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranādin, it was still merely sitting at home in retirement. A monk’s spirit and bearing are like those of a king—what evidence is there for this?
After a long silence, he said: "Miaoshan’s straw raincoat; Zhizhe’s staff."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When encountering objects, there is no obstruction; when raising the eyes, everything is contrary. The field is stable and secure, yet there is no path for turning back.

But tell me, how is it that throughout the sands of the Ganges, manifestation and concealment are uninterrupted? In a single phrase, how is this so? After a long silence, he said: "The affairs of the abbot are many."
As expected, he forgot.
He ascended the hall and said, "Maitreya, the true Maitreya. Holding up his staff, he asked, "Is this real or false?
Is there anyone who can say so? If there is no one, do not say that I, this mountain monk, am deceiving you all. With the staff slung over his shoulder, he said, "Heaven!"
Above there is no heaven; below there is no earth.
Entering the hall: Before a single bubble has arisen in the great ocean, [the Master] draws a line with his whisk and says: "Six segments of Kūn (earth), three continuous lines of Qian (heaven).
If you intend to blink your eyes, it will be donkey-year, donkey-year.
The Buddha entered nirvana on the same day as the birth of Bodhisattva Wonderful Light. He ascended the hall and said: "Born beneath the twin śāla trees, he passed away beneath the twin śāla trees.
Birth and death do not concern one another; each is merely a path traveled. Nevertheless, setting aside for a moment the matter of the coffin revealing his two crossed feet, tell me, everyone:
why does Bodhisattva Wonderful Light have the surname Liu? He gave a shout.

Ascending the hall: On this morning of the first day of the New Year, all things are renewed. For the patch-robed monk, to receive blessings in accordance with the season is not merely to blend with the light and mingle with the dust.
The cypress tree; the three pounds of flax; on the head of dead firewood, one releases the springtime warmth.
Ascending the hall, he said: "This winter has been bright and warm; the plum blossoms have all opened. A man of the way beneath the forest has plucked one or two buds;
he perceives only their lovely fragrance, yet knows not whether they will bear the 'soup-stirring' fruit. Why? Because there is still snow remaining."
Ascending the hall: "Tranquil and unmoving, yet responding and penetrating all. A mangy horse tied to a withered post. "Tranquil yet constantly moving, penetrating without being prompted.
In the four directions and eight corners, there is no net to ensnare. Without descending from the meditation seat, a single shout deafens the ears.
It does not hinder one’s playful engagement within the sea of human affairs.
Ascending the hall, he said: "All sounds are the Buddha’s voice; all forms are the Buddha’s form. Three parts of the day have already passed;
throughout heaven and earth, all are busy with spring. To let the springtime go by is a failure; it breaks one's heart to see the spring pass.
In the peach orchards, the nightingale cries—whom does it intoxicate as it dwells beside the flowers?"

Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally and said, "Prolonged rain does not hinder the farmers. He struck the ground once with the staff and said, "In spring sunshine, there is much to enjoy and admire.
Not bound by the Dharma, nor seeking liberation through the Dharma; not revering those who uphold the precepts, nor hating those who violate them;
not valuing long-standing practice, nor disparaging beginners: in every place there is water in the well; in whose hearth is there no smoke? Although...
"However, one might as well move a mountain, but one cannot change one's nature. [The Master] threw down his staff and said, "And it rolls back into the mud and water again.

On the first day of the fourth month, he ascended the hall and said: "Without passing through the City of Transformation, one overturns the Treasure Place; yet this is still but the pleasure of the journey. It is...
"You people, you have broken your staffs and hung up your alms-bag pouches; have you truly returned to the essential point?
You must know that beneath the three rafters is not the place for you all to settle yourselves; upon the long benches is not the place for you all to eat gruel or rice;
on the level ground is not the place for you all to practice walking meditation; and within the latrine is not [the place for you]."
"O you all, regarding the matters of great and small," he said, picking up his staff and saying, "The staff! Unconsciously, it leaps for joy with hands dancing and feet stomping.
Coming forward, he planted the staff on the ground and said, "The summer retreat is near."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Ancient and present forgotten, the paths of sage and ordinary man cut off—yet one still remains within the thicket of brambles.
Few are those who meet on the golden palace floor. Whether in hell or heaven, go forth as the master wherever you are. He struck the meditation staff and said:
"The high is appropriate; the low is also appropriate."
Ascending the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival, he held up his staff and said: "Whether it be medicine or not medicine, I take it up at hand as it comes.
It kills and it gives life, its wind blowing through the eight directions. Even if it were Mañjuśrī or Vimalakīrti, they could not do without this one dose. He struck the ground with the staff.
Ascending the hall on the birthday of the Great Being Shanhui (Śūraṅgama): "In the Tuṣita Palace, he could not hold it fast; within the mountains of Songshan, he borrowed a site to open his field.
Heaven and earth are entirely mud and water—how much more so when he comes as the one to succeed in this life?
Is there anyone who can hold fast to the boundaries? If there is none, he strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and says: "The Great Being has finished preaching the sutra."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Looking inward at the mind, the mind has no mind;
looking outward at the form, the form has no form; looking afar at things, things have no thing. Shuanglin remembered when, as a child going to school, one day he suddenly mastered the four tones.
Unconsciously filled with joy, he cried out, "I understand! I understand! But tell me, what did he understand?
The ruler bestows grace upon the people; his meritorious deeds are engraved upon the ritual vessels and tripods. How vast is the distance between them?

Upon breaking from retreat and ascending the hall, that phrase which cannot be uttered even with one’s full strength—whether it be south of the Yangtze or north of the river—the head of the patch-robed monk’s sack has already opened.
Before the staff is even lifted and before the straw sandals are even donned, he has already traveled throughout the four great continents.
"It is understood. How can you express it? If you cannot, the Twin Trees will speak for themselves. He then made a gesture with his hand as if brushing his eyebrows and asked, "How much is there?"
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "If you can grasp the meaning right here, then movement and stillness are one and the same, and there is no gap between this and that.
You will naturally be able to fully embody both movement and stillness, and fully embody both going and staying.
Should it be otherwise, picking up the staff and the straw sandals would be like a silver mountain and an iron wall."
Ascending the hall: Head touching heaven, feet treading the earth. Having come up upon hearing the sound of the drum, how much of your pride has been diminished?
It is better to kill yourself than to let others kill you; it is better to investigate yourself than to investigate others. The myriad phenomena of the universe are your very own teachers.
The myriad phenomena of the universe are your very selves. It is truly laughable that Pòzào Duò of Mount Sōng, being composed of nothing but mud and clay, would further claim to "break" and "fall.
Why do this? [The Master] takes up his staff, strikes it down, and says: "Arise!"

Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: the golden circle and the chestnut burr; the forge melts and refines. If you can swallow it through and penetrate it, even dull iron and stubborn copper will be transformed.
Baizhang needlessly boasts of being deaf for three days.
Dharma’s Memorial Day: Ascending the Hall. Dividing skin and dividing marrow to deceive the blind and deaf; he has defiled the Bear Ear Peak of Mount Song.
Carrying his single sandal back to the Pamir Mountains—where, as a thief, could he not be encountered?
Ascending the hall, he said: "To transcend verbal expression, iron mountains lie across; to sever verbal expression, the thoroughfare is overgrown with weeds. After a long silence, he said:
"Since childhood I have observed the fast; now I am old."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Two arise because of one; yet do not cling even to that one. This is the birth of the first yang.
From the place where you have shed the nest and cut off the net, bring forth a single phrase."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The oriole grows old and the flowers wither; the affairs of spring have already passed. Most bright-eyed monks miss it.
The breeze carrying the fragrance of the *lián* flower refuses to let it pass; through ten thousand doors and a thousand gates, it passes all at once.
Striking and bumping against things—who is at fault? It cannot be changed, yet I must test you. He struck the meditation seat and said, "Fault!"
The Buddha’s Birthday. Ascending the hall, he said: "The handle of the ladle has entered the hands of everyone; do not follow after delusion and sink yourself away.

Throughout heaven and across the earth, there is no deviation. As soon as the Yellow-Faced Gautama emerged from his mother’s womb, he went straight ahead—yet even he could not do without this one ladleful of foul water.
He struck the meditation staff once and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: On the ninth day there is no white wine; one eats their fill of yellow chestnut cakes. Upon the solitary peak at the very summit, the two eyes are raised even higher.
Unaware and unknowing, suddenly the cap falls off. The autumn wind is fierce! The autumn wind is fierce!
Ascending the hall: Busily, busily indeed! A fine steed has its fill of the bright day. Clenching the teeth with determination, he overturns the very axis of the earth.
The gods dare not rebuke him; the ghosts dare not weep. When the World-Honored One enters hell, Devadatta emerges from hell.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The single, firm, and dense body manifests within every mote of dust. Why is this? Only when the leaves fall does one know autumn.
Every person has blood beneath their skin; it pierces through the nostrils and replaces the eyes, yet they remain unaware and unknowing.
He let out a shout.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "To see it once is to see it; why trouble yourself with such entanglements? When the General does not mount the bridge, the valiant warrior does not don his armor.
Furthermore, what need is there to speak of Hanshan’s water buffalo—'four today, eight tomorrow'?
A monk asked Yantou: 'What is it like when one encounters a fierce tiger on the road? [Yantou] replied: 'Press! (Za!)"
Ascending the hall to thank the two ranks of officials and the various storehouse supervisors for their collection of offerings: The establishment of all dharmas is the absence of all dharmas;
this is True Suchness, the unsurpassed True Suchness. Spontaneously, one attains mastery over the mundane and supramundane dharmas, with Vasubandhu to the left and Asanga to the right.
To the south of the Heavenly Terrace and north of the Five Terraces, the kitchen, storehouse, monks’ hall, triple-gate, and Buddha hall stand four high and three wide.
With its eight-sided, translucent structure, guests and hosts mingle, all together preaching this Dharma. The Sanskrit sounds are pure and elegant, bringing joy to those who hear them.

Winds blow in their proper season, rains fall in their proper season; the grain is harvested in the fields and the granaries are filled. People beat upon the earthen tiles and sing songs, together rejoicing in non-action. Grasping the staff...
The Staff said: "Tell me, how about this staff? It can act as the master of the myriad phenomena, yet it does not wither with the four seasons.

When Xie Cui, the Head of the Administrative Office, ascended the hall, [the Master] entered the infinite and emerged from the inexhaustible, firmly seizing the vital ford: head upright, tail straight.
"Correct. Now tell me, by what is this verified? One, two, three, four—intersecting vertically and horizontally.
Leaving Bao Lin Temple to go to Chengtian Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture, he ascended the hall and said: "Ten thousand li of mountains and rivers, a single sky of bright moon;
at the tip of the staff, there is neither lack nor excess, neither 'that' nor 'this. He held up his staff, descended from the seat, and said: "Return my East!"
Recorded during the journey westward.
Compiled by the attendants Jingqiu and Zhijin for the *Lecture Record* of Chengtian Nengren Chan Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture.
In the Buddha Hall, he lifted up his sitting mat and said: "When gathered, it completely gathers the great earth; when spread out, it covers the entire trichiliocosm.
Now, the Yellow-Faced Gautama has no way to hide his body."
Seated upon the square measure of the hall, he opens the crown of the heads of a thousand sages and seizes the very bottom of the three miserable realms.
This nostril of yours, all of you, is entirely in the hands of this mountain monk. (He strikes the ground with his staff and says: "In a single stroke, I have pierced it through!"
A Provincial Edict: The Vajra Circle and the Thorny Jujube. To recognize these is the official seal of the patch-robed monk; it is the very furnace of creation. A Prefectural Memorial:
Seeking a pearl in red water is still a treasure of the human world; sung forth amidst the clouds, it is by no means a mystical discourse beyond the ordinary.
Within just this much, how shall one comprehend it? At the gateway of non-duality, take this up with earnest care.
Preface to the Mountain Gate: Before the Peak of Emei, behind the Jade Green Basin. Word by word, phrase by phrase—this is not to deceive you with mere written words.
Pointing to the Dharma seat: "Severing the summit of Vairocana, I do not follow Śākyamuni. He lets out a shout. "For now, stay downwind."

Ascending the seat, he offered prayers for the Emperor. (The questions and answers are not recorded. He then said: "The waters and sky are vast and open; the gate to the bustling marketplace stands wide.
Whether coming from the south or the north, cast aside the mounting platform at the entrance. A thousand gates and ten thousand households—all are places where the Tathāgata walks."
The patch-robed monks are rough and unrefined; they have no rules and no standards. A sweet melon is sweet from stem to tip;

a bitter gourd is bitter from root to blossom. Ultimately, how is it? After a long silence, he said: "With single-minded devotion they face the North; through ten thousand turns they flow toward the East.

[The Master] raised the case of Mingjue going to Xuedou after having arrived at Chengtian. A monk asked: "I do not ask about the Patriarchal intent coming from the West; I ask about the matter of the Northern Dipper concealing its body."
"How so? Xuedou said. "A fellow who takes the head for the tail. The monk said, "Please, Master, answer the question. Xuedou said, "The imperial decree is strict in the Western Heavens.
The Master said, "Xuedou drives a spike into his head and pins him down at his feet; every beat is the imperial decree, accomplishing all worlds.
Do you wish to recognize this monk? It is like Duke Ye painting a dragon."
Small Assembly. Holding up his staff, he said: "The total functioning of the Great Utility leaves not even a hair’s breadth behind.

Linji was solely intent on driving slaves; Deshan was solely intent on employing maidservants. Bajiao’s total functioning involved both giving and taking away—vainly building a ten-thousand-li defensive wall against the barbarians.
Yunmen, unable to restrain his impatience, flung it toward Xuefeng’s wide-open mouth. This mountain monk has no power to resist the wind, yet he does not dare [to speak]."
Like a tiger pouncing and a dragon soaring, he handled [the staff] sideways and upside down.

From the time he first traveled abroad until his recent departure from the Double Grove (Śāla Grove), crossing ridges and traversing sands, propping up the East and supporting the West—he gained his strength entirely from it. Now that he has come over the river, he washes his feet and boards the boat, arriving here without moving a step.
He thought this staff could be leaned against the wall; now the three beats of the drum have ended, and the assembly—

They arrived like clouds. Furthermore, the words were flavorless; the speech was flavorless; the Dharma was flavorless. Yet, he still troubled the staff to strike a small seat. He planted the staff and said:
"Even so, there is ultimately a point that remains unsatisfactory. Why? 'A slight gift brings resentment.
[He] raised the case of Master Shending opening the hall and addressing the assembly, saying: "When this mountain monk traveled as a pilgrim, I had no 'right cause' (zhengyin)."
I was simply waiting to go into the city of Dongjing to listen to a sutra or treatise in a quiet room at an ancient temple, passing my time in that manner.
Unexpectedly, while traveling to Ruzhou, I was blown by a gust of karmic wind onto Mount Shou, where I saw an old monk upon a curved wooden chair.
At that moment, I could not hold myself back and prostrated three times before him; it has been thus ever since.
"I regret it, but it cannot be undone. The Master said, "Shendeng opened his eyes and lost his footing; he fell into the pit at Shoushan. It was very much like a mute man eating a bitter melon.
Since you then prostrated three times before him, what was there to regret? This mountain monk [says this] from the beginning of the Jiading era."
There is likewise no true cause. Wandering as a single flavor, one has failed to reach a point of connection amidst the rivers and lakes.
Before Mount Taibai, an old monk struck a blow right where there was no connection, shattering the beggar’s nest;
even until now, it has become increasingly beyond reach.
Thank you, special messenger, for inviting these two monks to take their places in the hall.

The Dharma taught in Maitreya’s Tuṣita Heaven Palace, down to his final descent as the Regent Bodhisattva, is explained exactly as it was before, without the slightest variation. But tell me: on what basis do you say this?
It was indeed thus. He took up his staff and said, "A messenger, a messenger! You have not disgraced your mission.
[He then] thanked the Rector, the Head of the Monastery, and the old acquaintances. Ascending the hall, he said: "Xinghua struck Kebin—planting grain does not produce beans.
Although it required diligent cultivation, one must still know that there is something beyond it. Xinghua’s staff—Chengtian was not without reason for this; it was not 'not so'."
Setting it aside, I shall bring it forth. Since we have met a man of the mountains, let us speak of mountain talk.
As Xueya entered the hall, it was as if the earth shook and flowers rained down. But how can this compare to returning to the hall to warm oneself by the fire?
Xuedou is much like one who closes his door and seeks a livelihood; he has seized hold of the entire universe and the great earth, leaving you no place to turn or shift. *A!* It shatters Cai!
The city of the state has been completed.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Letting go at the precipice; sleeping on the grass beneath the clouds. Turning south into north across the four quarters and eight directions.
In a place where Buddhas and Patriarchs have not passed, and where the ancients have never arrived—how does one practice there? Three times nine is twenty-seven; blowing at the fence."
The Double-Reed Pipe.
On the eighteenth day, ascending the hall: Open the eyes of midnight and see the stars of midnight. Throughout heaven and across the earth, who does not do so?
What kind of Way has the Yellow-Faced Old Gautama accomplished? Examine!
Xie Liaoyuan ascends the hall: In a sandalwood forest, a lion’s den—a place where one cannot remain crouched—is precisely the moment for a somersault.
Only when every trace of smoke has vanished can it be brought forth. It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha; let no clear-eyed monk treat this with negligence.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The smoke from the Wu palace has cooled and the waters stretch far away; the waist-deep snow of that day has not yet melted.
Today is the twenty-fifth of the twelfth month; today is not yet the New Year’s morning."
Ascending the hall: It is the beginning of the year, the beginning of the month, the beginning of the day. With the commencement of the New Year, all myriad creatures come forth into life.

When Bodhidharma came from the West, he pointed directly at the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature, one attains Buddhahood. One flower blooms and five petals unfold; the fruiting occurs naturally.
These two distinct parts are now gathered back into the preceding section.
Taking leave of the two classes of assembly, he ascends the hall. One sits, seven walk; three crosswise, four upright. A person of great capacity carries this fully upon their shoulders.
But tell me, what is it they carry? Puhua’s bell and clapper; Yangqi’s donkey.

Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: From antiquity to the present, the lamps have been passed down in succession; throughout the earth and under the heavens, lamp after lamp continues without interruption.
This serves to illuminate the meaning of the true mark (*dharmatā*). Today is the fifteenth day of the first month.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Awakening to the Way by hearing sound. He struck his staff on the left side and said, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, go over here!
"Illuminating the mind by seeing form. He struck his staff on the right side and said, "Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, go over here!
"Ascending to the precious abode without moving a step. He struck his staff in the middle and said, "Under the feet of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, you should give him one..."
A Needle. Do you all wish to know where Chengtian has landed? Shaking his head, he speaks of ease before courtiers; with hands at play, he circles the board against laymen.
A letter from Master Bianshan of Tiantong arrived;
he ascended the hall and said: "Unfolding and rolling up, appearing and disappearing within the sea of birth and death—[it is] stone."
Fire cannot reach it; a flash of lightning cannot pursue it. Master Chengtian’s feelings for his brother were deep;
today he once again sheds these two rows of tears for the sake of Venerable Bianshan. Seeing it thus, one knows that no one in the world can do anything with this old man.
Ascending the hall at Nirvana Temple, he claimed preeminence at the end; in vain did he stride across the red earth. Rubbing his chest, he addressed the assembly:
"To the very end, one must suppress private interests. Thus living, thus dying—flowers and birds laugh without ceasing year after year. Zen monks possess their own golden bones.
The Abbot of Lingyin, Longzang, ascends the hall: "In years past, there was a song of deceptive emptiness; at the head of a rapid torrent, a bird builds its nest.
One wonders how many hands have transcribed this scripture—where there is no contradiction, yet contradiction exists. Today, as I look upon it at Chengtian, where is there any contradiction?
Every word reveals the ultimate truth; every sentence flows toward the source. Clouds rise on the Southern Mountain, and [the rain falls] in the North.
It rains in the mountains. Always wearing tattered straw sandals, the spring chill is piercingly sharp. I pray that you, the Abbot, enjoy ten thousand blessings.

Ascending the hall, he said: "When it is cold, all under heaven is cold; when it is hot, all under heaven is hot. Having penetrated beyond the barrier of cold and heat, when has one ever left the nest?
I think of how, when it is hot, one seeks coolness; when it is cold, one burns firewood. For no reason, one is called 'Zhaozhou' by others."
The Ancient Buddha.
Master Xie Shan, the Librarian Dāvinna, ascends the hall: "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, awakening by oneself without a teacher is the second phrase.
It cannot be fully explained by the entire Great Canon of Teachings; it cannot be struck out even under ten blows of the mallet. He looks around.
The attendants said, "What about the first phrase?
Kaibian then ascended the hall and said: "The trees have fallen from the thousand crags; the autumn sky is as if washed clean. At this very point, you must be able to turn your body around."
One can shift the stars and replace the constellations; turn the positions and reverse the mechanisms. At the top of a hundred-foot pole, not even a speck of dust stands.
If one can take a single step forward here, then killing and giving life, releasing and seizing, will be mastered with total freedom. Mount Sumeru has no summit; the vast ocean has no bottom.
Leaning on his staff, he said: "Chengtian Monastery has both tea and soup."
Master Xie Huiri ascends the hall: "Kāśyapa’s samādhi—Ānanda did not know it. Hearing the name and seeing the face—the sword has long since been lost.
Dragging the plow and trailing the oxen, they compete over who is first and last; Yangqi’s nostrils are missing half."

Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival, [the Master said: "Each person possesses their own radiance; yet when one looks for it, it is not seen, shrouded in darkness. Holding up his staff, he said: "Is this not radiance?
Striking the incense stand, he said: "Every sound and sight is clear and distinct. What would you call 'darkness'? He continued:
"In the triennial great examination, the hawks and eagles soar through autumn. Holding the staff horizontally across his chest, he asked: "Tell me, is this..."
What is the topic? He lets out a shout.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall. A biting wind sweeps the earth; the fierce cold is intense. The brazier trembles; the meditation seat trembles.
Before the firewood has even reached it, there is nothing at all. If your robes are thin, please return to the hall to warm yourselves by the fire.

Entering the hall: To reject external objects is supreme; to pursue external objects is inferior. At the base of the wall or the root of the fence, seeking seams and looking for cracks—when you step with confidence, the great earth sinks level.
This is the very substance of empty space; one realizes the body of a Mara King. (He hurls down his staff and says: "It turns out!"
It is, however, the "tortoise-nose" of the South Mountain. Entering the hall:
"On the auspicious first day of the first month, harmony begins; all things of fortune arrive in abundance. For us patch-robed monks, what need is there to speak of their "arriving in abundance"?
At the tips of the hundred grasses, the weapons of war are laid aside; at the crossroads of the city street, one plays freely and unrestrainedly. Jingqing Zhi—

Whether one enters the Buddha-dharma or not, there is loss of benefit. All are like those who embrace the bridge pillar to wash themselves. Holding his staff horizontally across him, he said: "Do you see?
The mountains and rivers cannot be fully traversed; the spring rain falls at no fixed time."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The single melody of Yunmen. On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, today is the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month.
You all claim to be guests in the gate of the patch-robed monks; tell me, what is this 'single melody of Yunmen'?
If you cannot say it, this staff will instead cause you all to be struck with awe and alarm. Why is this so? On the thirtieth day of the eleventh month."
It is right here before one’s eyes.

On the occasion of the festival commemorating the birth of the Heavenly Founder, he ascended the hall and said: “Heaven and earth have manifested their auspiciousness, and the Sage has descended. His grace moistens the four seas, and his virtue covers the myriad kingdoms.

For the man of the way beneath the forest trees, when sitting there is the meditation board and the *pútán*, and when in use there is the staff and the whisk—none of these are anything other than [the manifestation of that grace].”
Looking up to respond to the Sage’s grace, today I offer this single phrase of praise. But how is it so? This mind—outside of this mind, there is no other mind.

[This was spoken] upon ascending the hall to thank the Vice-Abbot, the Head of the Monastery, and the Head of the Quarters. "Tian Ku'er, how extraordinary! With a single stroke of the hoe, he struck—"
Breaking up clods of earth: the old monk of the entire earth has his skull shattered; sitting once and walking seven times, he unifies the internal and external.

Beneath the green pines, within the bright window—though jade palaces and crystal towers may exist, they are not the ultimate. Distinguishing every fraction to determine the weight, a single drop reveals the vast ocean.
He cried out in a loud voice, "The story of the staff remains! Leaning on the staff, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: "The Wheel of Dharma was turned three times throughout the great trichiliocosm; that wheel is originally and eternally pure.
In Pingjiang, they produce lanterns as the ground of the Way. Everyone knows that the Tathāgata Lamp-Light resides within your eyes and ears, turning such a wheel.
Why then do you not know it? [He lets out a shout.]
Ascending the hall, he said: "Thus have I heard: The rivers and mountains are beautiful on this late-day sun; the spring breeze brings fragrance to the flowers and grasses.
When the Buddhas appear in the world, they are blind and deaf; when Bodhidharma comes from the West, he is blind and deaf;
when monks gather in clusters and masses, they are blind and deaf. If you are such a man, then before the black bean has even sprouted, you must accept and practice it. (Thirty)
After several years, he finally came to know. But tell me, what did he know? His eyes were blind and his ears were deaf.
A letter from Master Dachuang of Lingyin arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "The void bursts asunder; the mountains and peaks dance.
The tongue is pulled out and the plow is driven—every evil deed is exposed. He took up his staff and said: "Chengtian shall give him another thirty blows of the heavy stick. Do you understand?"
"Do you know where this staff falls? [He said: "I dare not fail my elder brother, Kāśyapa. He ascended the hall and said:
"The realms of boundless lands do not separate self and other by so much as a hair’s tip; ten ages of past and present, from beginning to end, do not depart from the present moment.
When a monk hears this, he understands; when it is raised, he knows. The spring breeze blows vast and wide; the spring day..."
"Slowly... Now tell me: at Nālandā Monastery in India today, how many people have lost their nostrils?
If you do not know, Xiangtai shall take the blow for you. He struck Xiangtai once with his staff.
Descend from your seats.
An old acquaintance arrived during the assembly at Mount Miaofeng; together they cast a cauldron. Ascending the hall: At the summit of Mount Miaofeng, he searched for seven days without finding him.
Suddenly, on another peak, he took hold of his hand. He is truly like being forged from cast iron—his accomplishment is ineffable.
One may speak of the Buddha-work in the world of Fragrant Accumulation; yet, though so, the practitioner remains beyond the green mountains.
On the first day of the fourth month, he ascends the hall: Where the iron whip points, battle clouds spread; when one’s strength is exhausted, the mountain is even more sublime.
Furthermore, the lion’s backward leap—east, west, south, north—has no fixed destination. Midsummer is simply midsummer; for the patch-robed monk...
For what reason? All ends here today. After a long silence, he said: "How can one blame him?

[He then] thanked the master for presiding over the whisk. On the occasion of the birthday of Lady Huiganfu, he ascended the hall and said: "The True Spirit is without merit, yet its merit transcends the workings of creation.

The True Sage is without form, yet its form encompasses empty space. Acting through expedient means to gather and transform beings, he correctly guides from within and instructs from the side; like the wind passing through, the grass bends."
Yan: "The jade turns and the pearl revolves. Cause every person to turn toward this place, so that they may eat their fill of the flavor of the Dharma. He joined his palms and said, "I am ashamed.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Buying a black old woman—how did Yanhou obtain them for three coins? Coming and going empty-handed, the Old Barbarian!"
His movements and stillness were not yet clear. Entering the water, he did not stir the waves; entering the forest, he did not move the grass. Set this aside for a moment:
it is like snatching food from a tiger’s mouth or plucking a pearl from the jaws of a black dragon. But how about this? "The official will not allow even a needle."
Baomiao ascends the hall: He drives away the oxen of the plowman so that the crops may flourish; he takes the food from the hungry man so that everyone may be satiated and snoring contentedly.
Now tell me: Is Baomiao’s reading of the sutras and nurturing of the seedlings the same as this, or is it different?
If you can say it, you may realize the ocean of the *Cintāmaṇicakra-samādhi*; if you cannot, you will have brought shame upon Chengtian.
Bānxià ascends the hall.
Looking at the pavilion, he strikes the pavilion; surging east, submerging west; entering the water, entering the mud; piercing skin and penetrating bone.
At the crossroads, the Stone Daring One suddenly understands the phrase of turning around, and laughs at the falcon soaring through the vast heavens. The Great Master Bodhidharma’s eye—
His eyes bulged. He ascended the hall and said: "The realm of the Great Man—when the Buddhas and Patriarchs speak of it, it cannot be fathomed; when Mañjuśrī realizes it, it is profound stillness;

when Samantabhadra realizes it, it is layered multiplicity. When the Bodhisattva of Boundless Body arrives here, there is no place to exercise his supernatural powers. Chengtian [Temple] heads toward the clamor."
In the marketplace, he throws down a brick. Holding his staff upright, he says: "When one leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven.
To the two classes of assembly, he ascends the hall: "The function of the useless is of immense utility; the merit of the meritless is of vast achievement.
Spontaneously, it is like a dragon finding water, or a tiger relying on its mountain. The springtime within the alchemical vessel is unlike that of the human world."
Offering incense on the anniversary of the passing of Zen Master Zhe’weng: "The entirety of boundless space is the post-nirvana manifestation of Chan Master Fuxin of Mount Jing;
the entirety of boundless space is the Dharma seat of Chengtian. How can it be arranged? How can it be offered to?
Today, at Chengtian, tears flow from my heart in deep sorrow as I attempt to paint this very space. [He] picks up the incense.
He said: "Do you see it yet? Amidst the sound of the mountain stream and the colors of the mountains, there is a single piece of withered, rotten firewood.

Yuantong Zhongzhou arrived and ascended the hall (he was the successor of Wunian). He said: "From the gate of the ear, through the samādhi of perfect illumination, the conditioned mind attains mastery.
It falls eastward and topples westward; the different manifests as the same, and the small manifests as the great. But what about that which does not involve the eye’s forms or the ear’s sounds?"
"Sound! Where do you meet him? Wuli ji luo. Chuanzi hui. When the old friend from Jingci arrived, [Dongshan] ascended the hall and said:
'For a clever monk, what need is there to seek a handle? Where the foot is planted, not a blade of grass grows; when the eye is fixed, Buddhas and patriarchs are swept away.
Now tell me, on what do you rely? You do not love the South Mountain; you love..."* *Note: The text appears to be incomplete at this point.*
The Turtle-Nose.
When the Buddha ascended the hall for his final sermon at the Veṇuvana Garden, one cannot find death within life; beneath the twin śāla trees, one cannot find life within death.
[Hitting the back of his head with a锥 (awls)]—he plants his staff upright and says: "Is this life? Is this death? Rely!
[The Master] leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.

He ascended the hall and said: "In the southern provinces and the northern provinces, there are ten thousand threads and a thousand heads. A fishing line dangles in the water; a paper wick has no oil.
The Crane Spirit flies up into the heavens; the Earth-Dweller rides a yellow ox. In the great ocean, there are ten extraordinary things that have never yet been spoken of."
Dust and weeds rise from the bottom of the sea; the waters of the thousand rivers flow backward. In Vimalakīrti’s chamber, there are thirty-two thousand lion thrones.
With a snap of his fingers, he says: "Withdraw!"

Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: set down body and mind. Benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom—the Yellow-Faced Gautama searched the heavens and groveled on the earth.
On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, it is called "entering the retreat. When walking east, one does not see the benefit of walking west.
A letter from the late Master Donggu of Lingyin arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "The orthodox does not establish the mysterious; the partial has nothing to which it may attach itself.
For thirty years, he has walked among those of different species. As for the final word: 'The full moon at the ancient ferry. Now tell me, did Master Donggu come and go, or not?
The night boat turns its prow toward the crystal palace; white birds fly to roost in the shadowless tree."

To the elders who have established this field for the assembly hall: Truly, all that was previously lacking is now present. One’s own fields and lands are forever lost to one's own mastery; all that was empty is now filled.
The original deeds of ownership belong entirely to the person themselves. Every inch of land is gold; every single grain is ten thousand grains.
Whether it be the prison of heaven or the prison of the earth deities, join your palms in praise and say: "Namo to the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, who acts as the donor of the Dharma."
O Bodhisattva.
[He] thanked the Head Seat Jingci and ascended the hall to pray for rain: "A mere span of cloud gives rise to layered vapors, already possessing the power of vast diffusion.
All eyes gaze upon the clear sky; this is not to be compared with mist or fog. The Head Seat has traveled the pilgrimage routes—the Head Seat has arrived! He has fallen [into the net]."
Second. Look, look! But tell me, what is it that you look at? "The clouds move and the rain falls. He ascended the hall and said:
"At the summit of the solitary peak, there is no path for emerging. At the crossroads of the street, there is likewise neither front nor back.
Old Blind Shaveling Linji and the Dull Baguaid of Mingzhou do not issue their true commands; they fall eastward and collapse westward. If you people do not..."
Let it pass. A single stroke of "Heaven-Supporting" (Chengtian): within the crevice of the eyebrows, there is no way for you all to meet him.
*He gives a shout.* On the occasion of the Summer Retreat, he ascends the hall for a formal discourse. Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he says:

"The life-force of the Buddhas of the past and the administrative regulations of the Buddhas of the future have all been struck down at once. For the long period of one hundred and twenty days, by what means shall we abide? *He holds up the whisk.*
The Master said: "There is this very thing.

Upon retiring from the abbot’s quarters, he ascended the hall and said: "To pile up earth on level ground has existed since antiquity; when a thunderbolt strikes the blue sky, it is difficult even to avoid.
On the tip of the staff there is naturally the eye that penetrates all directions; the single realm of wind and moon is no ordinary matter."
Record of the Sayings of Chan Master [Name] of Chong’en Zishou Chan Temple on Mount Bai in Anjī Prefecture, compiled by his attendant. Buddha Hall:
Wooden frame with golden adornment—it is indeed like that; a blink of an eye, a raising of the eyebrows, from India to this land.
Occupying the chamber, he overturned Mount Sumeru and overturned the great ocean. Fishes and dragons underwent transformations; birds and beasts cried out in joy.
He lowered one foot and said: "For now, let the Buddhas and Patriarchs emerge."
The official document from the Prefecture states: "If one discusses this matter, it is like the jewel within a king’s topknot; it is not given away lightly.
Only when one’s eyes are sharp and clear can one know its place of origin."
The Preface to the Commentary: Within the conventional truth (saṃvṛti-satya), there exists the true noble truth (ārya-satya). This is like the eyes of the Yellow River and the mouth of the sea;
it is difficult to fully proclaim. Raising up the commentary, he asks: "Do you see? The Great King arrives!"
He pointed to the Dharma seat. Where the Elephant King has trodden, foxes and rabbits leave no trace; when the moon in the water appears, the wind and clouds naturally differ.
Taking a brisk pace, he said: "Lift up your eyes!"
After the ritual for the Emperor’s longevity was concluded, he took his seat and said: "The four quarters are thoroughly penetrated; ten thousand streams flow toward the central source.

One phrase cuts off the current; all mechanisms of response are submerged. Is there anyone who can recognize the meaning within the hook? A monk asked: "Placing a blade of grass to establish a Buddhist monastery—"
"Excellence lies in meeting the occasion. The Prince specially established this monastery; how did the Master proclaim the Dharma? The Teacher said, "Listen well.
The student asked, "It may be called a phrase that startles the masses; when met with one who startles the masses, it is proclaimed.

When met with a person of extraordinary character, such an extraordinary matter is brought forth. The Teacher said, "Whenever you meet someone, simply speak in this manner. The student asked, "What about now?"
"Not a little," the Master said. "Bring me back that phrase which startles the multitude. The student asked, "What is the phrase that startles the multitude?
The Master said, "A clap of thunder too swift for the ears to cover. The student asked, "What is the extraordinary matter?

The Master said, "Therefore, at this very place, auspiciousness is gathered. The student said, "I remember how the World-Honored One offered flowers and lit lamps at the spot where his hair was spread to cover the mud."

"How is it so? The Master said, "Entering the water, one sees the tall man. The student asked further, "When Dīpaṃkara Buddha pointed to the place where Śikhin had spread his hair, saying, 'This plot of ground is suitable for building a Buddhist monastery,' what was that about? The Master said, "There is bait on the hook.

The student asked, "At that time, among the assembly there was an elder named Xiānzhū who held up a measuring pole and planted it at the spot where [Dīpaṃkara] had pointed, saying, 'The construction of the monastery is complete. What was that? The Master said—
[The Master] said: "Waves surge and peaks stand. The student asked: "At that time, the devas scattered flowers and praised, saying, 'This elder possesses great wisdom.
Master, you say, 'Praise indeed, praise cannot reach it. Today, the Patriarch-Founder has completed the construction of this Brahma-shrine;
how would you, O Monk, praise it? The Master said: "The void can be measured and the wind can be bound; none can describe this Buddha."
